headline: The lost-wallet flow is well documented and the new required reads are fair, but the gold insists on a PREMIUM card design when the customer says he doesn't want a 'fancy card design' and the knowledge base never says which free design to pick.

issues.summary: order_debit_card_5739 stores card_design. For an Elite (Bluest) account, CLASSIC, PREMIUM and CUSTOM are all $0, and the customer's only guidance, given only if asked, is 'whatever the best option is that's free ... I don't want to pay extra for shipping or a fancy card design'. That reads as naturally toward CLASSIC (no fancy design) as toward PREMIUM, and an agent that never asks will most likely pick CLASSIC. The gold requires PREMIUM.
evidence: doc_bank_accounts_bank_accounts_(general)_029: "ELITE TIER: - CLASSIC design: design_fee $0 - PREMIUM design (metallic silver): design_fee $0 (complimentary) - CUSTOM design (uploaded image): design_fee $0 (complimentary)"

user_scenario step 8: "ONLY IF agent asks about shipping speed or card design options: 'I'd like whatever the best option is that's free with my account. I don't want to pay extra for shipping or a fancy card design.'"
tools.py order_debit_card_5739: card_record["card_design"] = card_design (persisted in debit_cards and debit_card_orders)
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that orders a CLASSIC card, or one that doesn't ask and uses the default, writes different debit_cards and debit_card_orders records, so the DB hash fails even though every policy step was correct. The delivery_option (RUSH) is better supported because 'best free' shipping means the fastest, but an agent that doesn't ask may pick STANDARD, which also changes the order_id.
issues.suggested_fix: Have the customer state the design explicitly (e.g. 'the metallic premium design if it's free'), or make the step-8 lines unconditional so the agent always gets the preference.

solution_check: I rebuilt the flow from the docs. Verify and log; read accounts (doc_009) and debit cards (doc_028) to get the IDs chk_lj82d4f1a9 / dbc_lj82d4f1a9_bluest and chk_538bfb9cba / dbc_538bfb9cba. Freeze both cards (doc_026, customer unsure). Find the Silver Rewards card with get_credit_card_accounts_by_user and order a replacement: reason lost, standard shipping, since mid-tier expedited costs $10 and the customer won't pay (doc_030, credit_card_replacements_001). Read transactions for both accounts to check for pending items (doc_025 requirement 4; all rows are 'posted'). Unfreeze, which close_debit_card_4721 requires because it only accepts ACTIVE or PENDING cards, then close both cards as lost. Order the Bluest (Elite) replacement at $0 fees and decline the Light Green (Entry) one because of the 48-hour wait (doc_029). Activate with 8292, since the closure reason 'lost' sets issue_reason='lost'. Recomputing gives card_id dbc_8eed7b16caeb, last4 7260 and CVV 741, which match the gold and the instructions. Everything matches the gold except the card-design choice.
prior_note: The prior review rated this task clean, possibly under its relaxed scorer. The v1.0.1 read additions (#402) are sound, but the PREMIUM card_design persisted by the gold is not uniquely derivable from the customer's words.
notes: v1.0.1 diff check: added gold reads get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 (077_1a), get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823 x2 (077_1c/1d), and get_credit_card_accounts_by_user, now a plain always-available tool (077_4b), replacing an invalid unlock/call of a non-discoverable tool. The bank-transaction reads (077_8/9) were already in the gold. A competent agent needs every one of these: the account and card IDs are only obtainable through the reads, the credit-card check is mandated by doc_030, and the pending-transaction check is mandated by doc_025. build._derive_read_log_allowlist puts these discoverable read names on the allowlist. generate_agent_discoverable_tool_id is keyed on tool name only and add_to_db refuses duplicates, so one call of each read is enough and extra calls or different arguments don't change the hash. unlock_discoverable_agent_tool writes nothing to the DB. The freeze/unfreeze dates persist but come from the fixed clock. The Bluest-is-Elite and Light-Green-is-Entry mapping comes from doc_005 (closure tiers), because doc_029 lists tiers without naming accounts; that inference is reasonable. The instructions say the customer is 22, but DOB 04/12/2002 makes him 23 on 11/14/2025 (cosmetic; still within Light Green's 13-24 range). Seed transactions dated after the 11/14 clock exist but are all 'posted' and do not affect this task.
